 Cedric Coward (wrist) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Coward, who played 28 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, is dealing with a sprained left wrist. With the doubtful tag, he’s more likely to miss Friday. If Coward sits, reserves like Scotty Pippen Jr. and Jerami Grant would get more offensive opportunities. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cedric Coward had 7 points (3-of-6 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists, a block, and a three. 
 It wasn’t the best outing for Coward who had five fouls in this game. He was being drafted in the 80’s and through the 90’s in redraft leagues. Obviously, you would want more at that price point, but it didn’t happen tonight. He’ll have his next opportunity against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome accumulated 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five assists and one block over 15 minutes in Monday’s preseason win over the Hawks. 
 It’s notable that Jerome got the start over Scotty Pippen Jr. during Memphis’ preseason opener and he responded by pouring in 10 first-half points on 4-of-8 shooting as Memphis exploded for 82 points in an impressive opening half. It’s fair to wonder whether Jerome can build off his initial success with the Grizzlies last year when he averaged 19.7 points while shooting over 42 percent from three-point range after finally making his season debut in late January. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward added 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in the loss to the Warriors on Sunday. 
 Coward was, again, one of Memphis’ top performers on Sunday. He struggled inside the arc but was lethal from beyond it, draining all five of his three-point attempts before finishing tied for a team-high 19 points. The second-year guard also fared well on the glass and as a facilitator in the loss. If he can increase his three-point efficiency and take a step forward as a passer, he should be in for a good sophomore season as it pertains to fantasy basketball. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward finished Saturday’s win over the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers. 
 The results in Summer League don’t mean a great deal, but teams with a chance to take home the title usually ramp things up a notch toward the end of the week. Coward has surpassed 20 points in each of his last two games, with Saturday’s effort helping push the Grizzlies into Sunday’s title game. Given the players Memphis has moved on from within the last year, the franchise is embarking on a new era, and Coward is expected to be one of the leaders. And his skill set is such that he could be an incredibly valuable player in fantasy basketball, especially for those competing in category leagues. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward tallied 23 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Hawks. 
 Coward and the Grizzlies rolled to a 96-64 victory, guaranteeing themselves a place in Saturday’s semifinals. The second-year guard was efficient offensively, shooting well over 50 percent from the field, with his final line lacking only a blocked shot. With the Grizzlies embarking on a new era, the tandem of Coward and lottery pick Cameron Boozer will be asked to lead the way, and they possess the highest fantasy ceilings on the current roster. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward accumulated 17 points (7-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks. 
 That makes two double-doubles in as many games for Coward, who also dished out four assists. The combination of injuries that limited him to 62 games as a rookie and the Grizzlies beginning a new era without Ja Morant could explain why Coward is still playing in Summer League. Still, it would be unsurprising if he were shut down at some point. Due to the changes made by the Grizzlies’ brain trust over the past season and this summer, Coward will have a higher fantasy ceiling in 2026-27. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward notched 17 points (5-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Making his first appearance in Las Vegas after shoulder surgery sidelined him last summer, Coward finished Friday’s 97-96 victory with a solid double-double. As was the case in Salt Lake City, the Grizzlies wing struggled with his perimeter shot on Friday, shooting 1-of-5 from beyond the arc. However, Coward provided value as a rebounder, defender and playmaker. With the Grizzlies turning the page from the Ja Morant era, Coward is one of the players who will figure prominently in their rotation next season. That makes him a more valuable fantasy basketball option, especially if Coward can improve his perimeter shooting. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward finished Monday’s loss to the Jazz with 23 points (9-of-21 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound, one assist, one steal, three blocks and three three-pointers. 
 While he shot 33.8 percent from beyond the arc as a rookie, shoulder surgery that ended his final college season prematurely factored into Coward’s shooting struggles last season. He was only 3-of-12 from deep on Monday and is now 12-of-34 from the field through two summer league games, but Coward did clean things up from inside the arc. The Grizzlies’ wing shot 6-of-9 from two on Monday after missing all four of his attempts on Saturday. Given the number of shots he’s gotten up so far, Coward may not see much time in Las Vegas later this week. 
 Cedric Coward 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #23 
 Cedric Coward contributed 11 points (3-of-13 FGs), eight rebounds, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Thunder on Saturday. 
 Coward didn’t have his most effective shooting performance in the first game of his second summer league, but that clearly wasn’t an issue during his rookie season. He was able to make an impact on the glass and defensively, while he shot 3-of-9 beyond the arc, he was 0-of-4 on two-point attempts. Coward shot 72.9 percent in the restricted area last season and 47 percent on two-pointers, so this shouldn’t be a lingering issue for him. He may not see many more appearances this summer. 
 Jerami Grant 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 #9 
 The Grizzlies have acquired Jerami Grant and Kris Murray from the Trail Blazers for Ja Morant. 
 After four seasons, Grant’s time in Portland has come to an end. The veteran forward has been the subject of trade rumors each of the last two seasons, but nothing got done before Monday. Grant appeared in 57 games last season, averaging 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.4 three-pointers, shooting 45.3 percent from the field and 81.4 percent from the foul line. His departure from Portland frees things up for Deni Avdija and Shaedon Sharpe on the wing, but both will have to find their opportunities within a rotation that includes Morant and Damian Lillard.

 Jalen Suggs finished Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 14 points (6-of-12 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
 Fantasy managers don’t have to worry about a game’s outcome, so those rostering Suggs may have been pleased with his night. The Magic point guard recorded a complete stat line against the Timberwolves, shooting 50 percent from the field. Depending on Paolo Banchero’s status after injuring his right ankle in the third quarter, Suggs may have more scoring opportunities in Sunday’s game against the Knicks.

 Paolo Banchero (ankle) finished Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 14 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and one steal.
 Banchero and the Magic fell to 0-2 on Friday, and his right ankle injury made matters worse. While crashing for a rebound early in the third quarter, Banchero collided with teammate Jalen Suggs and tweaked his right ankle. Banchero returned after a quick trip to the locker room, but the team decided halfway through the fourth quarter to shut him down for the rest of the night. The Magic visit the Knicks on Sunday; if Banchero can’t play, Tristan da Silva is the most likely replacement in the starting lineup.
